text.p: Holidays in London and Hong Kong restrained commodities trading on Monday, although there was a rally in wheat futures and a correction in prices for oil and refined products.

CBOT wheat futures closed higher on a rally in corn and soybean futures, traders said. Gains were limited by news Egypt over the weekend bought 200,000 tonnes of wheat from France, more than the 150,000 tonnes it bought from the United States. Rumors circulated late Friday that Egypt over the weekend would be in the market for U.S. wheat. Also gains were limited by nearly-ideal harvesting weather in the U.S. spring wheat growing region. Wheat futures volume was estimated at 18,000, up from 11,024 Friday. Wheat closed four to 7-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with September up 6-1/2 at $4.59-1/4 a bushel.

New York precious metals futures ended mostly higher Monday, on moderate volumes, while London and Hong Kong markets were closed for holidays. "We saw some trade and fund buying on a day in which it was probably easier to make the high print with London and Hong Kong out, but there was some good quality fund buying seen," North American Equity Services floor trader John Geraghty said. COMEX December gold ended up $1.30 an ounce at $394.50, after seeing a two week high at $394.60 intraday on total estimated volume in the gold strip of 11,000 lots. In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted late at $389.20/389.70, from a London afternoon fix Friday of $387.50, and a New York close Friday at $388.00/388.50.

NYMEX crude oil and refined products closed sharply lower, with gasoline prices hardest hit, amid a correction of the oil complex following a recent price run up, traders said. "We are in the midst of a correction to relieve some of the overbought condition we are in technically," said Tom Bentz, a trader with ING Derivatives. September unleaded gasoline closed down 1.60 cents to 61.62 cents a gallon Monday. All three legs of the oil complex hit contract highs in the prompt months last week, but profit-taking firmly took hold on Friday, traders said.
CSCE world sugar futures settled just above the day's lows after a volatile and technically-dominated session, floor sources said.

Early speculative buying fueled the spot-October contract above resistance at 11.94, where a double top has formed on the charts, to a high of 11.98. But the contract fell just short of the key 12.00-cent mark and succumbed to fund and trade selling, which pressured October to 11.64.

The market steadied towards the middle of the range and drifted lower for the remainder of the session. October finished 0.20 weaker to 11.65, having ranged from 11.98 to 11.63. March closed off 0.11 at 11.35, while the back months ended 0.10 to 0.08 weaker.
Dealers said today's close points to weaker prices Tuesday. "It definately puts us on shaky ground," one trader said.
He said the speculators could attempt to take out the stops below 11.60 and 11.65, they were unable to reach today.
Despite the losses, analysts said the longer term outlook remains to the upside, and see spot-October climbing to around 12.50.
The LCE was closed today for a public bank holiday.
